symbols.name: simultaneous butterfly layer
symbols.meaning: The map applied at once to one selected bit of each of d chunks, acting as a two-point butterfly on each selected bit.
symbols.quote: The simultaneous butterfly layer $H_0$ is the map that applies a two-point butterfly to one selected address bit of every chunk in one pass.

symbols.name: chunk count
symbols.meaning: The number of equal-width chunks, each with one selected bit, on which the layer acts.
symbols.quote: Here $d$ is the number of chunks, not the number of axes used on the transform page.

symbols.name: record length
symbols.meaning: The number of complex coefficients in each polynomial record stored at an address.
symbols.quote: Each address holds a polynomial record of $r$ complex coefficients, where $r$ is the number of complex coefficients in a record.

symbols.name: chunk length
symbols.meaning: The number of positions in each of the two chunks being interchanged.
symbols.quote: Swapping two chunks of $e$ positions each costs $O(Ve^\tau)$ for a fixed $\tau<1$, where $e$ is the number of positions in each chunk.

symbols.name: layer cost exponent
symbols.meaning: A fixed exponent below 1 that sets the power of d in the cost bound of the layer.

relations.quote: Intermediate values in the layer are exact [Gaussian dyadic numbers](gaussian-dyadic.md), whose real and imaginary parts have power-of-two denominators, each stored with $p$ bits after the binary point.
The layer acts on arrays stored in the [Frame of a vertex](frame.md) on each wire.
Applying $H_0$ to all $d$ selected bits is built by the [Tensor product](tensor-product.md) of the $d$ single-bit butterflies, so applying them one at a time in any order gives the same result.
